verdict.rationale: Fellow documents a public REST Developer API with API-key authentication, cursor-based pagination, and an OpenAPI 3.1 spec. The API both reads data (recordings, transcripts, notes, action items) and writes it (agenda append, prepend, find-replace and write; action-item completion and archiving; recording uploads), so an AI-native user can genuinely drive the product, and an llms.txt is also served. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, a published API changelog or deprecation policy, a sandbox/test workspace, and access without a paid plan or admin enablement.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The Developer API opens that data to you: transcripts, structured notes, and more, all available through standard REST calls.
All API requests must include a valid API key in the Authorization header.
Write a note's agenda and/or rename the note. Provide `content_fellow_markdown`, `title`, or both.
Mark an action item as complete or incomplete.
Upload a recording from a URL. Use this endpoint to bring an existing meeting recording into Fellow.
The Fellow Developer API uses cursor-based pagination for all list endpoints.
The API Reference and Developer Guide is available at: https://developers.fellow.ai/
